paper_title: Das Dilemma der Speicherverpflichtung im Gasmarkt: Optimiertes Marktdesign erforderlich
caption: Entwicklung der Gasspeicherfüllstände und Füllstandsvorgaben in Deutschland
model_annotation: The diagram illustrates the development of gas storage levels and storage requirements in Germany from January 1 to December 31, with the x-axis labeled with months and the y-axis representing percentage levels ranging from 0% to 100% in increments of 10%. Multiple lines are plotted on the graph, each representing a different year or range of years, including 2011-2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025, distinguished by various colors such as gray, pink, maroon, green, dark blue, and light blue. The gray lines for 2011-2019 show a general trend of decreasing from around 90% in early January to approximately 30% by early April, before increasing to around 80-90% by late November, with slight variations across the years. The colored lines for specific years exhibit similar trends, with the 2020 line starting at around 85% and decreasing to approximately 25% by early April before rising to around 90% by late October, while the 2021 line starts at around 60%, decreases to roughly 20% by early April, and then increases to about 70% by late October. The 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025 lines generally follow a similar pattern. Additionally, blue square markers are plotted on the graph, labeled as "Speicherverpflichtung" (storage obligation), showing values at certain points, including around 30% in early February, 80% in early October, and 90% in early November. A blue text box highlights that the current storage level in Germany is approximately 37%.
